scope: Fixed three-clock oracle representation comparison on every saved G31 pilot leg; no fitting, synthesis or GAF experiment

method.spatial_path: Identical G31 2049-point target-derived equal-arc path, float64, shared by all arms
method.progress: Normalized cumulative observed arc, float32 in all arms; constant-path progress is time/duration
method.relative_257: Frozen G22 positions/decode with 257 equally spaced relative-time controls
method.physical_1s: Control times [0,1,...,floor(T),T], unique terminal endpoint; interpolate with actual seconds
method.native_0_25s: Control times at all native .25 s samples; target-derived resolution control, not a learned model
method.output_and_position_errors: Original .25-second observation clock in all arms; no invented event-boundary coordinate
method.motion_metrics: Inherited G31 one-second cumulative-XY-arc speed/acceleration; same ten endpoints and support rules
method.native_auxiliary_metrics: Coordinate displacement / actual native .25s interval, then speed difference / interval-midpoint time difference; MAE/RMSE/max, separate from ten main endpoints and not simulator-reported speed
method.aggregation: Descriptive per-leg summaries and paired differences, lower error is better; repeated parent legs remain dependent; no confidence intervals
method.capacity_cost: Control-point counts are representation size, not a measured model-runtime or equal-compute claim

limits: All three arms use target-derived spatial paths, durations and control values unavailable at genuine generation time.
Smaller oracle error does not establish that a model can learn the longer sequence or that GAF helps it.

Integer-second motion metrics are aligned to the physical_1s knots; native .25s position, speed and acceleration errors plus the .25s control expose remaining within-second loss. Better one-second metrics do not establish that one second is universally sufficient.
No long or short leg is removed; unsupported short-leg endpoints remain explicitly counted.
One pilot with shared demand is not independent generation evaluation or a new-line generalization test.
Native-resolution control retains spatial discretization and float32 progress error and is not assumed exact.
